rows.title: Scope
rows.pointer: MduX renders content described by a device's own UI design; it does not itself define what that device's users see or how they interact with it in a specific clinical context.

rows.title: Normative references
rows.pointer: Read alongside docs/iso14971/, which covers the risk-management framework this standard's use-related risk analysis sits inside.

rows.title: Terms and definitions
rows.pointer: MduX has no mechanism addressing use error directly yet; the closest adjacent idea is rendered-truth verification (issue #16), which confirms *what is displayed* matches the compiled screen's specification, a precondition for a user being able to act on correct information at all.

rows.title: General requirements
rows.pointer: MduX provides no mechanism against this clause and cannot: applying a usability engineering process requires a device, its users and its use environment, none of which a rendering library has.

rows.title: Usability engineering process
rows.pointer: Device-level; MduX supplies no process, having no users of its own.

rows.title: Risk control as it relates to user interface design
rows.pointer: MduX's planned mechanisms attach to this sub-clause more directly than to any other in §4.

rows.title: Information for safety as it relates to usability
rows.pointer: No MduX mechanism, and the boundary is worth stating plainly: MduX renders whatever text a device gives it.

rows.title: Usability engineering file
rows.pointer: MduX supplies no usability engineering file.

rows.title: Tailoring of the usability engineering effort
rows.pointer: A manufacturer tailoring their effort may reasonably treat parts of a UI built on MduX differently from others; MduX neither makes nor records that judgement.

rows.title: Prepare use specification
rows.pointer: Entirely device-level information MduX has no visibility into.

rows.title: Identify user interface characteristics related to safety and potential use errors
rows.pointer: The step MduX's planned mechanisms attach to - @safety_critical annotations, requirement binding, locale text budgets (issue #15) and rendered-truth verification (issue #16) - none of which exists yet.

rows.title: Identify known or foreseeable hazards and hazardous situations
rows.pointer: MduX has no mechanism: a hazard is a property of the device and its clinical context, not of a rendering library.

rows.title: Identify and describe hazard-related use scenarios
rows.pointer: No MduX mechanism, and none plausible: a use scenario is a description of what a person does, which a library cannot enumerate for a device it has never seen.

rows.title: Select the hazard-related use scenarios for summative evaluation
Establish user interface specification
rows.pointer: A .medui source file (issue #15) is what a device's UI specification would be authored against, but the specification itself stays the manufacturer's.

rows.title: Establish user interface evaluation plan
rows.pointer: Device-level; no MduX mechanism, and none plausible: an evaluation plan is a statement about people and a use environment, neither of which a library has.

rows.title: Perform user interface design, implementation and formative evaluation
rows.pointer: For a device built on MduX, implementing a user interface *is* authoring and compiling `.medui` screens (issue #15).

rows.title: Perform summative evaluation of the usability of the user interface
rows.pointer: Rendered-truth verification (issue #16) is the closest adjacent idea MduX has, and it is worth naming the gap precisely: it confirms that a compiled screen renders the state it was given.

rows.title: User interface of unknown provenance
rows.pointer: **This is the clause an integrator is most likely to apply to MduX itself**, and it was missing from this corpus entirely until the numbering was verified.
